title: Symmetry-Preserving Local Representation for Short-Range Interaction in Complex Materials
authors: Hao Cheng, Tong Yang, Hao Wu, Haokai Hong, Zhongrui Wang, Shu Ping Lau, Wanyu Lin, Kay Chen Tan, Ming Yang
abstract: Modeling short-range interactions in highly disordered materials remains challenging due to the immense configuration space and the disruption of local symmetry in truncated theoretical models. Here, we propose a symmetry-preserving local representation framework that strictly enforces topological continuity and translational invariance via boundary passivation. Applied to high-entropy alloys, this approach autonomously unravels the nonlinear ligand effects modulating local reactivity and accurately captures coverage-dependent many-body interactions without explicit periodic expansion. By resolving the conflict between localized chemical environments and extended periodic boundaries, this framework not only reduces computational complexity by an order of magnitude but also provides a physically transparent paradigm for deciphering short-range order in complex condensed matter systems.
summary: This paper presents a novel, symmetry-preserving local representation framework, CG-NET, for modeling interactions in disordered materials like high-entropy alloys. By combining topological boundary passivation with symmetry-weighted sampling, it overcomes the limitations of traditional methods that struggle with both local disorder and periodic boundary conditions. This results in a highly efficient and physically transparent tool for deciphering complex many-body interactions in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: Modeling short-range interactions in highly disordered materials is challenging due to the immense configuration space and the disruption of local symmetry in traditional theoretical models.
main_result: The proposed framework significantly reduces computational complexity while accurately capturing complex physical phenomena like coverage-dependent many-body interactions and nonlinear ligand effects.
method: The authors introduce a Cluster Graph Neural Network (CG-NET) that enforces symmetry preservation and topological continuity using boundary passivation and multiplicity weights.
model_or_system: The framework is applied to complex condensed matter systems, specifically high-entropy alloys (HEAs), and is designed to handle disordered materials and interfaces.
key_observables: Adsorption energy, Formation energy, Conservative atomic forces, and the spatial dependence of nonlinear ligand effects.
important_parameters: The method achieves order-of-magnitude reduction in computational complexity and significantly reduces required graphical edges (77%-92% reduction).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that physical behavior can be captured by local environments augmented with deterministic, non-learnable boundary corrections (pseudo-nodes).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the method components, including topological boundary passivation and translational invariance enforcement. Other figures compare prediction fidelity (MAE) and VRAM usage across various datasets.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the CG-NET framework, details the techniques for boundary passivation and symmetry enforcement, validates its performance across diverse materials (HEA, OC20, etc.), and demonstrates its ability to extract physical insights like ligand effects from the latent space.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter ML, the rigorous enforcement of physical symmetries (translational invariance, local topology) mirrors the constraints often necessary when modeling quantum systems on finite or complex geometries.
